A consensus or guidance figure by itself keeps the judgement at the reference's rung; once other evidence has arrived it is never the reason to stay. Then derive the outcome the evidence implies: reported figures and guidance give a run-rate whose pace you forecast, informed by guidance, never the last quarter annualised flat; a quantified revision, a customer's demand number, a supplier's constraint, a confirmed delay or cancellation shift it. Guidance for the current or next quarter is the strongest forecast input. A management target for a product not yet shipping, or an ambition spanning years, is an input, not an answer: weigh time and execution (how many selling quarters remain, what volume and price the figure implies, what the company's own choices say) under the evidence requirement below; consensus is where the market stands, not the answer either. third_party_view and rumour move the forecast in proportion to their specificity (a number, a date, a named party): a research firm's shipment or revenue tracking with a number counts. A commitment or deal that is announced but not sized is sized from its disclosed comparable (the same programme's other deal, scaled by capacity or units); a figure no one states is derived from the accounting identities in the evidence when they allow it. A repeat, another outlet for the same claim, or an opinion that adds no new fact or calculation moves nothing. Missing confirmation alone is not grounds for the lowest or highest rung: an event not being confirmed is not confirmation that it did not happen.
- An evidence item that replaces another includes its predecessor for context, such as guidance revised from 12% to 25% growth. The predecessor is no longer evidence in force.

A theme marked "updated since this thesis was last judged" may change the conclusion; one that is not marked already stood at the previous judgement. When no themes are listed, theme_pushes is empty.
- Your conclusions must be consistent with each other and with the themes in force as shown: a share cannot be judged at zero while the policy that gates it is judged likely to open.

Every number an answer rests on is a figure; a number you judge rather than read or compute is an estimate, stated as yours. Explain whether the evidence as a whole favours one band before deciding whether or how much to adjust. Show support for the size or a justifying bound. If the passages lack the quantity asked, explain why a related figure fits the companies, period and quantity, and why your assumptions favour that band. If you can say only that the outcome might fall short or overshoot, not which band is more likely, answer unresolved and name what is unknown. Write explanations in English; preserve IDs and any quoted source text.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

e5309.text: The company has generated $164 billion in revenue from its data center segment in the first six months of fiscal 2027.
e5309.speaker: Harsh Chauhan, fool.com

e5310.text: That translates into an annual run rate of just under $330 billion for the full year.
e5310.speaker: Harsh Chauhan, fool.com

e5311.text: According to NVIDIA’s Aug. 26 press release, the company’s total revenues reached $96.2 billion in the fiscal second quarter of 2027, up 106% year over year and 18% sequentially.
e5311.speaker: Zacks.com

e5312.text: The Data Center business remained the key growth driver, with revenues rising 117% year over year and 18% sequentially to $89 billion.
e5312.speaker: Zacks.com

e5314.text: Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects profitability to remain strong and projects revenues to reach $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, in the fiscal third quarter of 2027, up 12% sequentially from the midpoint.
e5314.speaker: Zacks.com

e5320.text: Nvidia reported its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Aug. 27. Revenue for the quarter rose to a record $96.2 billion, more than double year-over-year (YoY).
e5320.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5323.text: Looking forward, Nvidia expects third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, which implies a range of about $106 billion to $110 billion.
e5323.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5326.text: In the fiscal year ended Jan. 25, 2026, according to its latest annual report, revenue reached approximately $215.9 billion. This was a massive increase of nearly 65.5% compared with the prior year.
e5326.speaker: fool.com (Erin Kennedy)

e5330.text: However, AMD is testing FSR Multi Frame Generation of up to 8X in newer drivers for RDNA 4 GPUs (via VideoCardz), and that might arrive sooner than expected and give it an edge over DLSS 4.5.
e5330.speaker: MakeUseOf, Shaheer Khan

e5331.text: Early partners include the startup The Matrix, which is adopting NVLink Fusion for its next-generation Raptor XPU to connect Vera and NVLink Switch racks, building a complete NVLink 72 architecture that incorporates The Matrix chip. Amazon AWS and Annapurna Labs are also collaborating with us to integrate custom IP into the base die of NVHBM, unlocking 30% to 40% of computing resources on their cu
e5331.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5332.text: In the AgentX benchmark, computational demand has increased by a factor of 100 on purely numerical tasks.
e5332.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5333.text: In fact, if you track the hourly instance rental rates for the A100—released at the onset of the COVID‑19 pandemic—you'll find that they have not declined over time but have instead risen, with demand remaining robust.
e5333.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5338.text: Huawei stacks them: its Atlas 960 SuperPoD, a cluster of more than 4,000 accelerators linked together via fiber optics, is meant to compensate through sheer numbers for what each chip concedes to the American company.
e5338.speaker: korben.info

e5339.text: One small detail though: this machine is notably more modest than the 15,000-chip monster mentioned last year. The chip is arriving earlier, but the cluster has shrunk.
e5339.speaker: korben.info

e5340.text: The group even admits it isn't producing enough to meet Chinese demand.
e5340.speaker: korben.info

e5341.text: the company is also open-sourcing its in-house equivalent, CANN, already compatible with widely used tools like PyTorch.
e5341.speaker: korben.info

e5352.text: Wall Street analysts expect Nvidia to generate around $411 billion in revenue in fiscal 2027.
e5352.speaker: supercarblondie.com

e5355.text: Nvidia's revenue in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 (ended July 26) rose 106% year over year to $96.2 billion
e5355.speaker: fool.com author Daniel Sparks

e5356.text: with $89 billion of that coming from data centers.
e5356.speaker: fool.com author Daniel Sparks

e5363.text: Nvidia grew revenue 106% year over year in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (a period that ended July 26), reaching $96.2 billion.
e5363.speaker: fool.com (Daniel Sparks)

e5364.text: Data center revenue climbed 117% to $89.0 billion.
e5364.speaker: fool.com (Daniel Sparks)

e5365.text: The company's year-over-year revenue growth rate has now accelerated for four straight quarters, moving from 62% last fall to 73%, then 85%, and now 106%.
e5365.speaker: Daniel Sparks

e5368.text: With revenue accelerating and next fiscal year's ceiling set by supply, today, I think, looks a lot more like the stalls the stock grew its way out of.
e5368.speaker: Daniel Sparks

e5378.text: According to some analyst models, SpaceX accounts for approximately 5% of NVIDIA's revenue.
e5378.speaker: finance.yahoo.com

e5383.text: Nscale stated that, as of the end of August this year, its in-house data centers hosted 7 megawatts of active computing capacity, while an additional 48 megawatts were operating in leased data center space, under contracts totaling $2.6 billion. Furthermore, 1.3 gigawatts of capacity is currently being prepared.
e5383.speaker: Cailian Press, reporting Nscale’s prospectus

e5384.text: Last month, Nscale signed a landmark agreement with Anthropic to lease capacity at its flagship data center in West Virginia. The six-year deal is valued at up to $45 billion.
e5384.speaker: Cailian Press

e5385.text: Nscale estimates that this data center, currently under construction, is expected to begin phased commissioning by the end of next year, with a total cost of approximately US$70 billion, including a 2 GW natural-gas-fired power plant to support its operations.
e5385.speaker: Cailian Press, reporting Nscale’s estimate

e5386.text: Snap is collaborating with Nvidia for access to an open-source extended reality AI platform that businesses can use when developing applications for immersive devices.
e5386.speaker: TechRadar

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

e5320.text: Nvidia reported its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Aug. 27. Revenue for the quarter rose to a record $96.2 billion, more than double year-over-year (YoY).
e5320.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5323.text: Looking forward, Nvidia expects third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, which implies a range of about $106 billion to $110 billion.
e5323.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5326.text: In the fiscal year ended Jan. 25, 2026, according to its latest annual report, revenue reached approximately $215.9 billion. This was a massive increase of nearly 65.5% compared with the prior year.
e5326.speaker: fool.com (Erin Kennedy)

e5330.text: However, AMD is testing FSR Multi Frame Generation of up to 8X in newer drivers for RDNA 4 GPUs (via VideoCardz), and that might arrive sooner than expected and give it an edge over DLSS 4.5.
e5330.speaker: MakeUseOf, Shaheer Khan

e5331.text: Early partners include the startup The Matrix, which is adopting NVLink Fusion for its next-generation Raptor XPU to connect Vera and NVLink Switch racks, building a complete NVLink 72 architecture that incorporates The Matrix chip. Amazon AWS and Annapurna Labs are also collaborating with us to integrate custom IP into the base die of NVHBM, unlocking 30% to 40% of computing resources on their cu
e5331.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5332.text: In the AgentX benchmark, computational demand has increased by a factor of 100 on purely numerical tasks.
e5332.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5333.text: In fact, if you track the hourly instance rental rates for the A100—released at the onset of the COVID‑19 pandemic—you'll find that they have not declined over time but have instead risen, with demand remaining robust.
e5333.speaker: Ian Buck, NVIDIA Vice President

e5338.text: Huawei stacks them: its Atlas 960 SuperPoD, a cluster of more than 4,000 accelerators linked together via fiber optics, is meant to compensate through sheer numbers for what each chip concedes to the American company.
e5338.speaker: korben.info

e5339.text: One small detail though: this machine is notably more modest than the 15,000-chip monster mentioned last year. The chip is arriving earlier, but the cluster has shrunk.
e5339.speaker: korben.info

e5340.text: The group even admits it isn't producing enough to meet Chinese demand.
e5340.speaker: korben.info

e5341.text: the company is also open-sourcing its in-house equivalent, CANN, already compatible with widely used tools like PyTorch.
e5341.speaker: korben.info

e5352.text: Wall Street analysts expect Nvidia to generate around $411 billion in revenue in fiscal 2027.
e5352.speaker: supercarblondie.com

e5355.text: Nvidia's revenue in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 (ended July 26) rose 106% year over year to $96.2 billion
e5355.speaker: fool.com author Daniel Sparks

e5356.text: with $89 billion of that coming from data centers.
e5356.speaker: fool.com author Daniel Sparks

e5363.text: Nvidia grew revenue 106% year over year in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (a period that ended July 26), reaching $96.2 billion.
e5363.speaker: fool.com (Daniel Sparks)

e5364.text: Data center revenue climbed 117% to $89.0 billion.
e5364.speaker: fool.com (Daniel Sparks)

e5365.text: The company's year-over-year revenue growth rate has now accelerated for four straight quarters, moving from 62% last fall to 73%, then 85%, and now 106%.
e5365.speaker: Daniel Sparks

e5368.text: With revenue accelerating and next fiscal year's ceiling set by supply, today, I think, looks a lot more like the stalls the stock grew its way out of.
e5368.speaker: Daniel Sparks

e5378.text: According to some analyst models, SpaceX accounts for approximately 5% of NVIDIA's revenue.
e5378.speaker: finance.yahoo.com

e5383.text: Nscale stated that, as of the end of August this year, its in-house data centers hosted 7 megawatts of active computing capacity, while an additional 48 megawatts were operating in leased data center space, under contracts totaling $2.6 billion. Furthermore, 1.3 gigawatts of capacity is currently being prepared.
e5383.speaker: Cailian Press, reporting Nscale’s prospectus

e5384.text: Last month, Nscale signed a landmark agreement with Anthropic to lease capacity at its flagship data center in West Virginia. The six-year deal is valued at up to $45 billion.
e5384.speaker: Cailian Press

e5385.text: Nscale estimates that this data center, currently under construction, is expected to begin phased commissioning by the end of next year, with a total cost of approximately US$70 billion, including a 2 GW natural-gas-fired power plant to support its operations.
e5385.speaker: Cailian Press, reporting Nscale’s estimate

e5386.text: Snap is collaborating with Nvidia for access to an open-source extended reality AI platform that businesses can use when developing applications for immersive devices.
e5386.speaker: TechRadar

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

e5013.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5015.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5016.text: Analysts expect earnings to grow 95% in 2027, 67% in 2028, 34% in 2029, and 12% in 2030.
e5016.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5018.text: Revenue for the quarter rose to a record $96.2 billion, more than double year-over-year (YoY).
e5018.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5022.speaker: barchart.com (analyst)

e5033.text: Last year, Nvidia's current flagship graphics card, the RTX 5090 , launched at a semi-respectable price of $1,999. e5034.speaker: BGR author Aaron Greenbaum, relaying TechRadar

You are a senior hedge-fund analyst judging the current rungs of a family of related number theses: one company's quantities that overlap, such as a total and its segment, a level and its growth, or a later year that rests on an earlier year's base. Use only the supplied evidence and themes in force. Each rung is your forecast: the outcome the evidence in force makes most likely at the due date, not the one it has proved.

- Judge every member from the evidence shown (what recent judgements relied on and what arrived recently) and the themes in force, as if for the first time. Earlier forecasts are not shown: whether a conclusion changed is compared afterwards.
- Judge each member against a reference: what the market expects for that question (consensus, the company's guidance, the stated plan or deadline). Say where the reference sits on its ladder. A consensus or guidance figure by itself keeps the judgement at the reference's rung; once other evidence has arrived it is never the reason to stay. Then derive the outcome the evidence implies: reported figures and guidance give a run-rate whose pace you forecast, informed by guidance, never the last quarter annualised flat; a quantified revision, a customer's demand number, a supplier's constraint, a confirmed delay or cancellation shift it. A target for a product with no shipments yet is discounted subject to the evidence requirement below; it remains a forecast when reaffirmed, and is taken in full only when you show what evidence puts the required volume in hand for the period. Build the family's figures once and read every member's outcome from them: a part cannot exceed its whole, a figure that spans several periods or products gives a question only its share, and a quantity the family shares has one forecast. Compare each outcome with its rung boundaries, and move when it crosses one.
- Weigh by tier and by novelty. Only fact can establish that a rung's outcome already holds; "not established" is a statement of confidence, never a reason to stay. Guidance for the current or next quarter is the strongest forecast input. A management target for a product not yet shipping, or an ambition spanning years, is an input, not an answer: weigh time and execution (how many selling quarters remain, what volume and price the figure implies, what the company's own choices say) under the evidence requirement below; consensus is where the market stands, not the answer either. third_party_view and rumour move the forecast in proportion to their specificity (a number, a date, a named party): a research firm's shipment or revenue tracking with a number counts. A commitment or deal that is announced but not sized is sized from its disclosed comparable (the same programme's other deal, scaled by capacity or units); a figure no one states is derived from the accounting identities in the evidence when they allow it. A repeat, another outlet for the same claim, or an opinion that adds no new fact or calculation moves nothing. Missing confirmation alone is not grounds for the lowest or highest rung: an event not being confirmed is not confirmation that it did not happen.
- An evidence item that replaces another includes its predecessor for context, such as guidance revised from 12% to 25% growth. The predecessor is no longer evidence in force.
- "Themes in force" lists the library's open theme theses (policy stages, shared quantities) with their current conclusions. They are our own judgements, never evidence: do not cite them in cites. Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

e5276.text: For the quarter ended Aug. 2, Broadcom reported $29.6 billion in revenue, up 86% year over year. AI semiconductor sales accounted for $16.7 billion, more than half of total revenue, and surged 221% from a year earlier and 54% from the prior quarter.
e5276.speaker: fool.com (analyst)

e5277.text: Management also outlined an aggressive runway: about $58 billion in AI semiconductor revenue for fiscal 2026, up 186% from the prior year, followed by roughly $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028, according to a Reuters report . e5277.speaker: fool.com (analyst), citing a Reuters report

e5278.text: Put side by side, Broadcom's forecast is clearly the more aggressive one. Its AI semiconductor revenue is projected to grow faster than Nvidia's on both a percentage basis and in absolute dollars.
e5278.speaker: Micah Zimmerman, fool.com

e5280.text: The company does not report a stand-alone "AI revenue" figure, but data center revenue ($89 billion in the latest quarter) is a reasonable proxy, since that business is overwhelmingly driven by AI computing demand.
e5280.speaker: Micah Zimmerman, fool.com

e5281.text: Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue to reach roughly $58 billion this year, then climb to about $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. In other words, Broadcom is forecasting one doubling, followed by another doubling.
e5281.speaker: Micah Zimmerman, fool.com

e5283.text: Broadcom's AI opportunity is more concentrated: it relies on a smaller number of massive customers building custom chips at scale, according to Reuters reporting, a model that can deliver exceptional profits but also carries greater risk if a major buyer pulls back or changes direction.
e5283.speaker: Micah Zimmerman, citing Reuters reporting

e5284.text: Broadcom may offer the more eye-catching near-term growth forecast, but Nvidia's slower-but-broader expansion could prove more durable over the long run.
e5284.speaker: Micah Zimmerman, fool.com

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.

Answer per the JSON schema: one calculation for the family and one answer per member.

id.description: Short and unique, such as F1; never a passage id.

measure.description: The quantity, such as revenue or capital expenditure; never its basis.

period.description: For example FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1, FY2027 Q1-Q3, CY2026, end of FY2027.

what.description: What the number measures. Where the request lists keys (outcome keys, shared quantities), copy them exactly.

kind.description: source: a number written in a shown passage's quote; computed: one operation on other figures; estimate: your judgement, with its assumption in basis_text.

basis.description: reported: an actual; guidance: the company's outlook; consensus: analysts' average; third_party: one outside party; forecast: this family's own forecast, on a computed or estimate figure only.

anyOf.description: A point. Give value, or low and high, never both.
A range, low at most high, with value null.
A range, low at most high, with value null.

unit.description: USD bn: money in billions of US dollars ($1.2 trillion = 1200; $500 million = 0.5). %: a percentage as its number (7.5% = 7.5). x: a multiple (double = 2).

anyOf.description: Source only: the passage whose quote holds the number.

Source only: a complete number exactly as the quote writes it, never a piece of a longer number, range or 'plus or minus' expression, with its currency and scale or its percent sign, and nothing else: '$4.5 billion', 'US$300 million', '$2.1bn', '40%', '-3%', 'double', 'twice'. The value is the number as written (a minus only when the quote writes one). A written range in full ('$3–4 billion', 'between $3 billion and $4 billion', '$3 billion to $4 billion'), given as low and high; a change written 'from $3 billion to $5 billion' is two numbers, each copied alone. '$4.5 billion, plus or minus 3%' in full, given as low and high or its midpoint as value. Only US dollars.
Source only: the qualifier the quote writes just before the number (or 'or more' / 'or less' just after); none when there is none.
Computed only: ids of figures, never passages, in the operation's order.

Computed only. sum(a, b, …) = a + b + … (one unit); difference(a, b) = a − b (one unit); product(a, b, …) = a × b × … (USD bn × x, x × x or % × x; never USD bn × %); ratio(a, b) = a ÷ b (same units give x; a ÷ x keeps a's unit); share(whole, percent) = whole × percent ÷ 100, the percent from 0 to 100; growth(old, new) = the % change, in one unit; apply_growth(base, rate %) = base × (1 + rate ÷ 100). sum and product take two or more inputs; the others exactly two. Never divide by a figure that can be zero. A range input gives a range: compute both extremes, a figure used twice taking one value; you may declare the midpoint as value. The figure equals the result within 0.5% (at least 0.1, or 0.05 for %). A sum never adds a figure of the part's quantity to one of the whole's for the same period (the whole already includes the part); a difference may take the part from the whole of the same period only to give the rest. A sum never adds one quantity for the same period twice. When a sum or difference combines periods of one quantity, write them FY2027, FY2027 Q3, FY2027 H1 or FY2027 Q1-Q3 (or CY likewise), and they make up the output's period exactly (Q1 + Q2 = H1; FY − Q1-Q3 = Q4).
Estimate only: the assumption, in words.
Estimate only: the ids of the figures and passages it rests on.

outcome_for.description: The members whose forecast this figure is: your own forecast (a computed or estimate figure with basis forecast, even when it agrees with consensus), exactly one for each member answered as a forecast, none for an unresolved one. Its what is the member's outcome key, in USD bn.

reference_for.description: The members for which this figure is the market's reference. It and every figure beneath it is a source or a computed figure, never an estimate or a forecast, and at least one of them is a quoted consensus, guidance or outside figure. A past period's reported share or multiple carried to another period (a quarter's mix applied to the year) makes it our comparison estimate, not the market's reference.

figures.description: The family's calculation. Use one forecast figure for each quantity and period, as a point or a range, wherever that quantity is needed (outside figures beneath it, or a point a final range rests on, are fine). Guidance may inform a growth pace: record the pace you forecast as an estimate, say why it applies, name the benchmark in rests_on, and use that estimate in the calculation. A rate computed from a shared quantity's guidance or outside figure is never itself an input of the calculation. To turn a total into a narrower quantity (data-center spending out of total capital expenditure), write the deduction or share as its own figure, or give a supported bound; never relabel a total as the narrower quantity. Figures name each other by id; no figure may depend on itself.

shape.description: forecast: a figure marked in outcome_for, a rung, and a reference (a figure marked in reference_for, or reference_unavailable). unresolved: why; rung and reference_unavailable null; no figure marked for it.

anyOf.description: Forecast only: the rung whose band holds the outcome as the code recomputes it (a band includes its lower edge, not its upper); for a range outcome, a band it overlaps, with the reason in reasons.
Forecast only, when no figure is marked as its reference: why.
Unresolved only: why the evidence cannot support a forecast.
